statement: Put k0 = 1 − d and Lraw = max{1, (1 + Q)/2, 1 + Crate}, (Q, Crate) = ( (q, q − J), curvature families, (0, c1), pure linear. Whenever the left label comparison in Proposition 5.4(iii) applies at v = u(j), the angular trace satisfies m(a, v) ≥ k0 + 2Γ + η(Lraw − 1) Lraw . 64 Fix a classical depth j, and let λj denote the random label encountered there on the final assigned law. Define Rj(v) = lim Hs(X(v) | λj), with conditional entropy averaged over that label random variable. Then Rj(u(j)) = 0, and lim inf z↓0 Rj(u(j) + z) z ≥ k0 + 2Γ + η(Lraw − 1) Lraw . (mr) These lower bounds hold on the same flattened law at every tested boundary prefix whenever λj predicts the boundary name; they are not assertions after conditioning on each individual label value. Under the small right-excess comparison, m(a, v) ≥ R′ j(v) almost everywhere. At typical classical j with Crate > 0, the following improvements are available: (i) If p∗(j) > b1(j), with the extra prediction persisting immediately to the left, replace Lraw by max{1, (1 + Q)/2}. (ii) If Q ≤ 1 and 0 < Crate < 1, an additional lower bound is k0 + 2Γ − Crateν(j), where ν is the mixed trace for the raw derivative, side y0, and graph B = b1.
